finding.claim: Unauthenticated OS command injection in GET /ping: req.query.host is concatenated into a string passed to exec(), which runs it via /bin/sh, allowing arbitrary commands with the server's privileges and returning output to the attacker.
finding.source: req.query.host from the query string of an unauthenticated GET /ping request (tools.js:6-7)
finding.sink: exec() at tools.js:7 with string concatenation "ping -c 1 " + req.query.host

trace.note: app.get("/ping") route registered with no auth middleware
req.query.host concatenated into shell command string and passed to exec()
On error, responds 502 with no body
On success, shell stdout is sent in the HTTP response, exfiltrating command output
app.listen(3001) with no host argument binds to all interfaces, making the endpoint reachable remotely

finding.guards_checked: No input validation or allowlist on host (tools.js:7). No authentication or authorization on any route (tools.js:4-26). exec used instead of execFile with an argument array, so no shell escaping (tools.js:7). No network restriction on listen (tools.js:28). Express query parsing does not neutralize the injection; array or object values still concatenate into an injectable string.

verdict.guard_found: none. tools.js:6 registers /ping with no auth middleware. tools.js:7 concatenates req.query.host into a string passed to exec(), which runs through /bin/sh, with no validation or allowlist and no execFile argument array. tools.js:28 calls app.listen(3001) with no host, so it is reachable beyond localhost. Express query parsing does not block injection: a string value passes straight through, and an array value concatenates into an injectable string.
verdict.reason: An anonymous remote client can send GET /ping?host=... and the unescaped value is concatenated into the shell command at tools.js:7, with stdout returned to the caller at tools.js:11; every other line in the trace matches the code.
